handoff.summary: Exact Windows SEA virtual-resource repair source 1223b27a410dc1b62c630cf045785f607d67c519 follows the independently approved first-float and awaited-session cleanup repairs. Fresh Windows attempt 5 passed the complete native suite and all four repaired budget cleanup gates, then failed in the root-A SEA smoke when the first embedded FLINT @native wrappers lacked nativeAvailable. Capture-only diagnostic 1 reproduced the failure without rebuilding or modifying proof evidence. Windows path.resolve had attached the current drive to root-relative SEA source and native-cache paths, but embedded resource lookup recognized only the undriven virtual root, so source hashing and native-wrapper loading fell through. Resource lookup now canonicalizes separators and removes only that optional drive prefix before matching the exact virtual-root boundary, preserving existing POSIX behavior. A focused mocked-SEA regression proves drive-resolved source reads, embedded native-wrapper loading, nativeAvailable, POSIX identity, and sibling-prefix rejection. At workspace fingerprint ce2242e77537d1bc253d13a505052d7fef5f0b08b9bdbdda3f24063cf00de6a9, focused Windows SEA, architecture, portable, strict-baselib, full changed-file, and all-contract receipt gates pass; the full changed-file gate includes the complete native suite and every budget.
